need: A feature audit must automatically manage its complete direct page, route-local or nested layout, feature-owned modal, and feature-owned drawer group through repair and fresh PASS 9+ evidence. A required shared-owner defect must be escalated to the Control Panel for explicit owner permission after remaining direct work continues; the feature task must neither stop silently nor duplicate shared behavior locally to evade scope.
negativeBoundary: Do not automatically mutate shared branches, global overlays, application shells, headers, navigation, or ancestor layouts. Do not let a scoped direct-owner PASS imply that an unresolved required shared owner passed, and do not force unrelated shared consumers into the feature mutation boundary without owner authorization.
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend audit guidance compiles every direct feature page, page-local or route-nested layout, modal, and drawer before capture and continues the whole group rather than stopping after one owner.
The mutation boundary accepts exact files owned by directly included modal and drawer owners while continuing to reject excluded shared branches and immutable ancestors.

A required shared-owner finding produces one Control Panel authority request naming exact files, visible defect, smallest proposed change, affected consumer regression matrix, and failed in-scope alternatives.
The runtime forbids recreating shared behavior inside a page-local component merely to bypass owner authority.
Feature PASS or 9+ remains forbidden while a required shared finding is unresolved unless the owner explicitly authorizes the shared mutation or accepts an evidence-backed debt or exclusion.

accepts: Keep every direct feature owner moving toward fresh PASS 9+ under Control Panel supervision.
Report a required shared-owner mutation to Control Panel and wait for explicit owner permission on that boundary.
Continue independent in-scope repairs before waiting on the shared authority decision.
rejects: Stop the entire feature without reporting the shared authority request to Control Panel.
Replace a shared modal with a page-local clone solely to avoid requesting shared-owner authority.
Claim feature 9+ while a required shared interaction still has fresh failing evidence.

review.rationale: Mock Interview exposed both failure modes: premature stop at a shared owner and an attempted local workaround that would duplicate shared behavior. The runtime needs direct-group persistence plus explicit Control Panel escalation.
